Eighteen comments

I usually play itr more like this
X: 1
T: Old Joe’s
M: 6/8
L: 1/8
R: jig
K: Dmaj
|:fAA AFA | BAF ABA | BdB AFA |Bcd efg |
fAA AFA | BAF ABA | BdB AFA | Bdc d3 :|
|: f3 efe | dBA d2e | faa a^ga |baf e2d |
f3 efe | dBA d2e | fAA AFA | Bdc d3 :|

It’s basically the same except I don’t hang on to the high B in the 4th bar of the B part. That changes the chord structure (more Gish than D), which is pretty much the only difference between the settings.

Bye for now

Old Joe’s, X:9

Taken from ‘A Fine Selection of Over 200 Irish Traditional Tunes for Sessions’, compiled by David Speers with a Forward by Matt Cranitch. I don’t remember hearing this before but, like many tunes in this book, seems to have fallen out of fashion - but deserving of a dusting down!

↳ Posted by Eubonian on January 3rd, 2019.

The Gullane

I know this tune as “The Gullane Jig”. If it’s called “Old Joe’s” then i’m not going to argue about the title. It’s a nice catchy tune for the flute.
